PullRequest.Title: Agents window: a chat's Changes tab shows its changes when no window shows the chat
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes a user-reported bug in the Agents window: a chat's Changes tab shows "No changed files" while its chat is not shown in any window.

## Problem

A Changes editor that names a chat (opened from that chat's Changes entry in a chat window) stays open as a tab after its chat leaves the window. For example, the chat tab was closed, another session's chat became the window's active chat, or the window was restored without the chat. The tab's header still showed the changeset picker and counts, but the body said "No changed files". The diffs only came back once the chat was shown again.

## Root cause

An Agent Host session subscribes to its chats' changeset, chat and session state only while a window (the main window or a chat window) shows the session (`createActiveSessionSubscriptionObs` gated on `isShownInWindow`). A Changes editor is not a window host. Once no window showed the session, the chat's changesets had no state, which the changeset reads as "no files, not loading", so the editor rendered "No changed files". #346763 made the editor resolve the chat its input names, but the data underneath stayed gated.

## Fix

The tab now behaves like a file editor: it stays open and shows its chat's changes whether or not the chat is shown.

- `IChat.observeChanges?()`, optional, modeled on the existing `observeCanvases()`. It keeps a chat's changesets and their changes observed while no window shows its session.
- Agent Host adapter: a per-chat observer count opens that chat's changesets (and the session state that names its default chat) while observed. Canvases reuse the same gate helper. The current-turn overlay keeps the session-visibility gate, because the turn changes it reads are only parsed while a window shows the session; a hidden chat therefore lists its Last Turn changeset's own files. The cloud sandbox task wrapper forwards `observeChanges`.
- `SessionChangesEditor` holds the observation for the chat its input names for as long as it has that input, also while its pane is hidden, so its diffs and their collapsed and scroll state stay as they are. It lets go when the input changes or is cleared, and when the editor closes; switching tabs in a group clears the input. Providers without `observeChanges` behave as before.
- While that chat's changes load, the editor waits for them as it already does for the active session. It hides both "No changed files" surfaces and shows its own progress bar, as the Changes view does, only while visible. The group's shared progress indicator isn't used, because the editor's input operation stops it once `setInput` finishes.
- The main window's session-level Changes editor (input names no chat) is unchanged.

## Tests

- `localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts`: the main and a peer chat of a session no window shows: no changes before `observeChanges()`, their changes and one live changeset subscription each while observed, and none after. Also an observed hidden chat lists its Last Turn changeset's files during an active turn.
- `changesMultiDiffSourceResolver.test.ts`: `observeChangesEditorChat` observes only the named chat once its session is known, does not churn when the chats change order, tolerates a chat without `observeChanges`, and releases on dispose. Loading is reported for chat-named editors only.
- `sessionChangesEditor.test.ts`: the observation lifecycle (kept while the pane is hidden and shown again; released on input change, `clearInput` and editor close; a session-level input never observes). With the real multi-diff widget, while the chat's changes are still loading after `setInput` stops waiting for them: the editor's own progress bar instead of "No Changed Files", only while visible, and the empty state once loaded.

RED: with the provider fix set aside, the new provider test fails: observed changes `[[],[]]`, live changeset subscriptions `[0,0]`. Each later review fix's test also failed without its fix: the hidden chat's Last Turn listed no files, and nothing visible showed while its changes loaded.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- `pnpm run eslint` on the changed TypeScript files: passed
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium` with `--run` for the three test files above: 651 passing, 0 failing
- `./scripts/test.sh --glob 'vs/{sessions,workbench/contrib/sessions,workbench/contrib/sessionChanges}/**/*.test.js'` (Electron): 10617 passing, 0 failing
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --glob 'vs/{sessions,workbench/contrib/sessions,workbench/contrib/sessionChanges}/**/*.test.js' --browser chromium`: 10342 passing, 0 failing

An independent review on a different model covered design, correctness, prior art, performance and lifecycle, security, compatibility, UX and accessibility, tests, and hygiene. It found three issues over two rounds, all fixed here: the Last Turn of a hidden chat, the multi-diff's own "No Changed Files" placeholder while loading, and the group's shared progress indicator being stopped by the input operation. It then approved with no known actionable findings.

## Live verification

Code - OSS built from this branch (before its last commit, which only replaces the shared progress indicator with the editor's own progress bar and is covered by the tests above), in the Agents window, on an isolated copy of an authenticated profile, launched in the background. Real Copilot sessions: A in `alpha` created `hello.txt`, B in `beta` created `world.txt`.

1. A shown in a chat window: its Changes tab lists `hello.txt +1 -0`.
2. B made that window's active chat, so no window shows A: the header reads "Branch · 1 File +1 -0" and the body keeps A's diff. Sampling the DOM every 40 ms never showed "No changed files", the placeholder or the empty state.
3. A's chat tab closed (the window holds only B): the diff stays.
4. Tab hidden (Files tab) and shown again: the diff comes back without an empty flash.
5. Quit and relaunch, which restores the window without A: the window shows only B, and A's Changes tab comes back with its diff.
6. Changes tab closed: no renderer errors from the changed code.
7. Main window unchanged: with A open there, its session-level Changes editor shows `hello.txt +1 -0`.

The "before" evidence is the original report's screenshot (Insiders): header "Versions · 12 Files +276 -85" over a "No changed files" body.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The hidden-input lifecycle is asserted by the added test, the changed predicate visibly omits `_paneVisible`, and the complete call path to refcounted protocol subscriptions, per-resource text-model creation, and eager per-document diff creation is explicit. Exact file counts and provider latency vary, affecting severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Agent Host subscription snapshots, up to two text-model references per changed file, and one DiffEditorViewModel/diff computation per file
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For a hidden editor the retained models and initial/background diff work grow linearly with the chat changeset's file count; each newly appearing file starts original/modified model resolution and a diff even though the pane is offscreen.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Background CPU and provider/filesystem I/O increase, and all resolved text models/diff view models remain retained while the hidden pane keeps its input, which can create responsiveness and memory pressure for large changesets.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: When no window showed the session, the chat changeset gate closed; the editor received no live file list (the reported empty-state bug), so the multi-diff did not keep resolving and diffing that hidden chat's files.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new observed source is gated only by `chat` and `_hasInput`, not `_paneVisible`, so a Changes editor continues the Agent Host session/chat/changeset subscriptions after `setEditorVisible(false)`. The resulting resource updates stay connected to the existing multi-diff model while the pane is hidden.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added return at line 258 keeps the observation alive whenever an input exists, including the explicitly supported `setVisible(false)` state; before this diff there was no external changes observation to keep the hidden chat's live file list feeding the multi-diff.
Findings.Title: Suspend change observation while the diff pane is hidden
Findings.Impact: Open a chat's Changes tab, switch the detail panel to Files (the new test explicitly keeps the input observed in this state), and let a background chat accumulate a large changeset. The offscreen editor eagerly resolves both sides and computes diffs for every file and retains those models until the input is cleared or the editor closes.
Findings.Evidence: `_observedChatSource` at the changed line remains defined solely from `_hasInput`; `setEditorVisible(false)` only updates `_paneVisible` at line 601 and does not release it. `observeChangesEditorChat` reaches the new Agent Host gate, which subscribes to session/chat/selected-changeset protocol resources. Those changes feed `ChangesMultiDiffSourceResolver.resources`; unchanged `MultiDiffEditorInput._createModel` maps every resource to `Promise.allSettled(createModelReference(original), createModelReference(modified))` at lines 225-230, and `MultiDiffEditorViewModel` eagerly creates a `DiffEditorViewModel` for every document and waits for every initial diff at lines 91-101 and 224-239. Thus visibility suppression only hides the progress bar; it does not suppress model resolution or diff work.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the current diff/view state cached while hidden, but gate the external observation (or propagation of new resources into the multi-diff model) on `_paneVisible`; resubscribe and refresh when shown. The existing hide path already saves collapsed/scroll state, so visible behavior can remain correct without performing new per-file model and diff work offscreen.

Scenarios.Scenario: A chat-named Changes editor is visible after no window shows that chat's session.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `setInput` establishes `observeChanges`, receives the session/chat catalogue and selected changeset snapshot, then resolves the multi-diff models; it waits for loading for at most 1 second and otherwise shows the editor-local progress indicator until data arrives.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to Agent Host session, chat, and selected changeset state and receive their initial snapshots/updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally three unique resource subscriptions for one chat editor (session, chat, selected changeset); duplicate references are coalesced by `AgentSubscriptionManager`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: When no window showed the session these subscriptions were gated off, so the chat-named editor incorrectly received no files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial snapshots are required to identify and display the correct files; `setInput` waits at most 1 second, after which loading continues with progress UI.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve original and modified text models and compute the multi-diff for each file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 2F model resolutions and F diff view models for F effective changed files, all initiated without a shared limiter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-file model and diff path already ran whenever the chat/session was shown and the Changes editor had a file list; the PR makes the list available when the editor itself is the presentation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is required to populate the visible multi-diff; initial display can wait for model/diff readiness or its existing timeout.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The selected changeset's effective file count F. The protocol catalogue is grouped by session/chat and only the selected changeset's file state is consumed; multi-diff model work is up to two model references and one diff view model per file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The subscription manager refcounts by resource, so duplicate session/chat references from the observable graph produce one wire subscription per unique URI. Multi-diff text model creation uses an unbounded `Promise.all` across files, with original and modified sides also started together.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm Agent Host resources reuse the refcounted subscription and warm text models can reuse model-service state. Cold entry fetches snapshots and resolves models. Failed protocol subscriptions are evicted on the next acquire; model promises are cached by resource pair for the input lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the gate, refcounted wire subscriptions, changes projection, and eager multi-diff model path were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent Host latency, model-provider cache hit rate, and typical changeset size vary, but the visible path needs this work to satisfy the feature.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding for the visible path: the new boundary is necessary to display the requested data, coalesced per resource, and loading is bounded/presented.

Scenarios.Scenario: The Changes pane keeps its chat input while hidden, such as when the detail panel switches to Files, and the chat changes in the background.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The work is off the hidden pane's presentation critical path. Because `_observedChatSource` ignores `_paneVisible`, protocol updates continue into the existing multi-diff model, which eagerly resolves models and computes diffs for new files even though rendering is hidden.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Keep receiving Agent Host session/chat/selected-changeset snapshots and updates while the pane is hidden.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three coalesced unique resource subscriptions per observed chat in the normal case, retained until input clear/editor close.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No external observation existed, so once no window showed the session these live subscriptions closed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off critical path while hidden; it competes with foreground work and is only useful for making a later show immediately current.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve and retain original/modified text models and compute diff models for the hidden editor's files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two model-provider resolutions plus one diff model per effective changed file; all file promises are joined concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Without the new hidden observation, the hidden chat supplied no live file resources, so this per-file model/diff work was not kept active for that chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Entirely offscreen while hidden; CPU/I/O and retained memory can delay unrelated foreground work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The retained state and background work scale with F files in the changeset; newly appearing resources start up to 2F cold model resolutions and F diff computations. Multiple hidden panes for different chats multiply this by their respective file counts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One wire subscription per unique session/chat/changeset URI is coalesced within a connection. Text model resolutions are launched via `Promise.all` for all resources, and each file starts both sides concurrently; there is no shared limiter on this hidden path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm protocol and model caches reduce cold I/O, but the editor deliberately retains model references and diff view models for the whole hidden-input lifetime. Cached resource pairs avoid recreating unchanged files; new files and cold restored resources still incur eager work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the added test proves observation survives `setVisible(false)`, the changed predicate omits visibility, and the transitive model code eagerly resolves and diffs every resource.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of large background changesets and provider I/O cost is uncertain, so severity is medium; the linear eager work and hidden reachability are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: preserving the hidden observation performs and retains linear per-file work offscreen; gate observation or resource propagation by visibility while retaining/restoring saved view state.

Scenarios.Scenario: The input changes, clears, or the Changes editor closes; multiple editors may observe the same chat.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `clearInput` sets `_hasInput` false, disposing the autorun-owned observation; editor disposal also releases it. Switching editor tabs clears the input before setting another one.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Unsubscribe Agent Host session/chat/changeset resources when the last editor/window reference is released.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one wire unsubscribe per unique URI when its refcount reaches zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no editor-owned reference to release; only window visibility controlled these subscriptions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cleanup is not on the input's visible rendering critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Observer count scales with live editor panes, but each chat gate is a boolean derived from a counter and the protocol manager coalesces same-resource references.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Multiple observers increment local counts; they do not create duplicate wire subscriptions for the same URI. Different chats have independent subscriptions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The protocol subscription remains warm while any observer or window host retains it and is unsubscribed at zero references. Multi-diff resource/model caches are disposed with removed resources/input lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both autorun stores and the protocol manager's zero-ref disposal were inspected, and added tests cover clear/change/close.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No material uncertainty in cleanup ownership; cancellation races are guarded by subscription-entry identity and refcounts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate lifecycle finding: cleanup and coalescing are correctly bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: A session-level Changes editor (no chat resource) or the chat loading progress UI is used.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session-level resolution keeps the existing active/session selection path and never calls `observeChanges`. For a chat-named editor, the added progress bar reacts to existing loading state and is delayed by 200 ms only while visible.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Progress work is constant per editor and does not scale with files. Session-level changes retain their prior file-count behavior.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is introduced by the progress UI or session-level branch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The progress state has no cache. Session-level changes continue using the existing observable caches and active-session subscriptions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the no-chat branch returns constant false loading and `_observedChatSource` requires a chat URI.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the progress bar is visible-only constant UI work, and the session-level editor is unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 9 changed files and transitive Agent Host/multi-diff paths. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity finding for eager per-file model resolution, diff computation, and retention while the pane is hidden. Protocol references otherwise coalesce correctly and release on input clear/close; visible loading behavior and the session-level editor do not add reportable regressions.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
